headline: Britain's flagship AI data center in Essex cannot get enough grid power and may not run until the 2030s.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: the Guardian broke the story on 24 Sep 2026 and TechRadar's 3 Oct piece adds nothing new.
importance_line: A project the UK government held up as proof of its AI ambitions is stuck behind a grid queue of 315 data centers, which hits the country's AI plans, Nscale's planned $35 billion flotation and anyone counting on faster connections, although the 2030s timeline is reported, not confirmed by the grid operator.
summary: The Guardian reported on 24 Sep 2026, in a story TechRadar relayed on 3 Oct, that the Nscale data center in Loughton, Essex, billed as the UK's largest AI supercomputer, will miss its 2027 launch because UK Power Networks has reportedly told the company the grid cannot deliver its 90 megawatts, enough for about 315,000 homes, until the early to mid-2030s. Nscale, a UK startup backed by Nvidia and preparing a $35 billion stock market listing, says it is "committed to the project" and is studying on-site generation, while regulator Ofgem counts 315 data centers waiting to connect, 73 gigawatts of demand against a national peak of 45.
notes: Pool source TechRadar credits the Guardian; the Guardian credits the newsletter Morning Intelligence for the first report of the power delay. Credit chain: Morning Intelligence first, Guardian the full report read here.
